title: fullcycle's INCOMPLETE summary names two of the three causes it fails a tree for: a tree it can search but not list goes unnamed
body:
## Problem

When fullcycle's artefact check cannot read a build tree, `_fullcycle_tree_listed` names each cause on its own line and marks the tree partial (lib/cmd/fullcycle:741-757):

- a directory in the tree it cannot search, which may be a target triple's (:742);
- a profile directory, `debug/` or `release/`, it cannot list (:750);
- a tree it can search but not list whose own `release/` holds no binary (:755).

Each sends the cycle to ARTEFACT CHECK INCOMPLETE at rc 1 (:1248-1249, :1328-1338). The summary's line for a partial tree (:1333) names only the first two: "A build tree could not be reached or searched, or a debug/ or release/ in it listed, or a directory in it that may be a target triple's searched". A tree that can be searched but not listed is neither unreachable nor unsearchable, so for the third cause the summary describes a failure that did not happen and points at the wrong permission: search, where the tree lacks read. The verdict is right; the summary's account of it is one cause short. The warning above it still names the tree, so nothing is lost, but the summary is the line a reader reaches first.

Found reading 0.1.9's note for vc before the cut: its 0168 entry said the summary names these causes, and the note was corrected at 891e700e to "each named on its own line, and the cycle fails as INCOMPLETE".

## Read at d7f2ed13 (v0.1.9), not run

The summary text at lib/cmd/fullcycle:1333 against the three warnings at :742, :750 and :755, and the path from each to `tree_partial` (:1244-1249). tests/unit/fullcycle.bats:3914-3933 holds the third cause's own warning and the INCOMPLETE banner, and no arm holds the summary's clause for it. Five arms read that summary line: :1505 and :1783 assert its closing phrase, "so that tree was not examined"; :1821 and :3021 refute parts of it; and :4017, in the arm for a profile under a triple that cannot be listed (:3999), asserts the clause for a directory that cannot be searched, the summary being one fixed sentence whatever the cause. When filed, this said only :3021 read the line. The page already names all three causes (lib/pages/fullcycle.md:39).

## Fix

The summary names the third cause too: a tree that could be searched but not listed, whose own `release/` held no binary. vc prefers this to narrowing the summary to the causes that held, since the page already names all three (2026-10-07).

## Done when

1. A tree the check can search but not list, whose own `release/` holds no binary, ends INCOMPLETE at rc 1 with a summary that names that cause; the arm, which may extend fullcycle.bats:3914, is red on d7f2ed13 first.
2. The other two causes still reach the summary, each held by an arm that asserts its own cause's clause.
3. The page at lib/pages/fullcycle.md:39 stays in step with the summary.

## Resolution

Landed at 2948439c on a green full suite (vc's, 2220 of 2220 ok, 0 not ok, .errors empty, seal 20261007-1151). The INCOMPLETE summary's sentence for a partial tree lists every cause a tree can be partial for, whichever held, on lines of its own:

```
    A build tree could not be reached or searched,
    or listed while its own release/ held no binary,
    or a debug/ or release/ in it listed,
    or a directory in it that may be a target triple's searched,
    or it lay behind a link that could not be followed exactly,
    so that tree was not examined (the lines above name each).
```

The second and fifth lines are new. A tree the check can search but not list, whose own `release/` holds no binary (`_fullcycle_tree_listed`'s third cause), and a tree behind a link that cannot be followed exactly (`_fullcycle_tree_gone` returning 3: a link loop, or a chain longer than the kernel follows) had no line there, and read as trees that could not be reached or searched. As vc preferred, the summary names every cause rather than only those that held; the warnings above it name the cause that held for each tree. The page, lib/pages/fullcycle.md, now names the link, one that cannot be followed exactly, beside the causes it already named. The summary's comment, `_fullcycle_tree_listed`'s header and the tree loop's block each say that a new cause gets a line in the summary, its words on the page and an arm that asserts the line, and `_fullcycle_tree_gone`'s header says that a new code of its own needs a branch in that loop as well, which otherwise names it out of reach.

Five arms assert their cause's line, each as a whole line through `assert_output_line`. Every line prints whenever a tree is partial, so each shows that the list names its cause, not which cause held; the warning each arm asserts beside it shows that:

- the tree that cannot be searched (0139's arm): the first line;
- the tree that can be searched but not listed (0168's arm): the second line, and the closing line;
- a directory in the tree that cannot be searched (0168's arm): its line;
- a profile that cannot be listed (0168's arm): its line, where it asserted the line for a directory that cannot be searched, a cause it never had;
- a link in a loop: INCOMPLETE and the fifth line, in an arm of its own, split from 0139's link arm so that neither the permission nor the kernel's link limit that arm rests on keeps it from running.

The fifth line is critic-shell's, from its review of the first build, which also asked for the comments to stop claiming one cause to a line and for each cause site to point at the summary and the page. Its review of the second scoped the INCOMPLETE block's own contract to its four flags, added the arm and `_fullcycle_tree_gone` to the pointers, put the page's link in the passive, since for a chain longer than the kernel follows it is the kernel that refuses, gave the loop its own arm, and three arm titles say the summary lists their cause.

Evidence, in ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-dc/0177/runs/, at 13bfae93 in the scratch clone (v2-arms-{bsd,gnu}-20261007-094420.log, v2-mutants-20261007-094420.log, v2-targeted-{bsd,gnu}-20261007-094420.log):

- Red on d7f2ed13: 266a5c17's summary, d7f2ed13's for this file, under the new arms turns all five cause arms red, each at its own line, under BSD tools and with GNU tools first on PATH. The two arms beside them that assert no 0177 line pass, the walk's and 0139's link arm.
- Green: the seven arms, 7 of 7 under BSD and under GNU.
- Mutants K1 to K8, all killed: each cause line dropped in turn, the closing line and the second line reworded, and the guard inverted, each applied, parsed, turned its aimed arm red, and was followed by the file restored to its committed bytes.
- The targeted run (fullcycle, helpers, contract, neutral, documentation, readonlygit, harness and help): 421 of 421 under BSD tools and 421 of 421 with GNU tools first on PATH, the tree clean before and after; the only skips are require_command's own two.
- critic-shell reviewed the first build (the fifth line, the comments, the pointers, the declared overstatement) and the second (one warning, five recommendations and two style points). This patch folds the second set in as the critic gave it, and was not reviewed a third time.

Declared limits:

- The summary lists every cause a partial tree can have, not only those that held; the warnings above it name the cause that held for each tree.
- "or listed while its own release/ held no binary" says more than the check knows when that `release/` cannot be listed, since dir_has_binary reads a directory it cannot list as empty. The warning above names that `release/` as one that cannot be listed, and the line for a `debug/` or `release/` that cannot be listed prints beside it.
- `_fullcycle_tree_gone` returns 3 when every name on the path is there, which a chain longer than the kernel follows explains, and so does a tree that came back between its tests, with no link on the way. That race is named, and now listed, as a tree behind a link that cannot be followed exactly. It fails closed, only the cause it names is wrong, and the words predate 0177.
